outcome.answer: Several papers address robust intent classification for chatbots. [2] focuses on noise-robust conversational intent classification under realistic conversational noise and finds attention pooling performs best, while mean pooling degrades performance. [1] studies intent classification for open-weight language models and evaluates robustness to realistic input perturbations, giving practical guidance under compute and latency constraints. [3] compares training-free and training-based intent classification methods and reports that training-free methods are generally more robust to mixed-intent and adversarial prompts.
